one_liner: A covariance-aware projection lifts in-sample Sharpe 26% on 100 S&P names, but loses to the plain Euclidean version in two of three walk-forward years.
Ten years of SEC Form 4 filings build an insider trading network whose coordinated clusters look nothing like shuffled or simulated nulls.
Across 7,286 rolling 10-day VaR forecasts, Bayesian networks breach on exactly the same three days as plain historical simulation.
Hidden Markov models with fat-tailed emissions pass distribution tests on SPY but fail out-of-sample on 11 of 30 individual stocks.
Welch-Goyal predictors only forecast the equity premium when the yield curve was flat or inverted recently; out-of-sample R-squared rises from 2.6% to 4.1%.
Fitting stochastic volatility in mean models by hidden Markov approximation runs about ten times faster than MCMC on four equity indices.
Rolling mean-variance and CVaR portfolios of 30 commodity ETFs beat equal weight on Sharpe and cut tail loss, with no trading costs charged.
Two Japanese bank mergers produced cumulative abnormal returns of 30% and 6%, though the estimate swings by half depending on the market model.
Ranking stocks by a put premium implied from their own price tree earns 3.7% yearly on the S&P 500, far under buy and hold.
An eigenvalue indicator from rogue wave physics flagged the 2008 VIX spike 18 trading days early, at 63% to 84% precision across three indices.
A quantum field theory fit to S&P 500 returns reproduces crisis kurtosis the Ising model misses and beats rolling regression on next-day AAPL error.
Log-periodic power law fits to Bitcoin and Ether place the 2017-2018 crash dates roughly right, fitted after the fact on a single window.
Swapping the covariance matrix for a multifractal fluctuation matrix gives the lowest drawdown and expected shortfall across four assets, reported only as figure bands.
A leakage-controlled LLM ranks equity style factors with rank IC 0.13, not statistically significant, and the traded version loses money after costs.
A standard self-similarity test rejects 47% of the time instead of 1%; a fractional-derivative version fixes it and puts stock indices near H=0.5.
Portfolios of the 40 most peripheral stocks in a noise-filtered correlation network earned Sharpe 0.81 against 0.51 for the market, 2010 to 2022.
An optimal local bandwidth for local Gaussian correlation buys little: adaptive tail estimates match the global ones within 0.01 on SPY, TLT and EEM.
Scoring three synthetic return generators on fidelity, temporal structure and downstream use puts TimeGAN ahead of a VAE and ARIMA-GARCH on every axis.
A participation-ratio rule finds a median of seven global factors in daily S&P 500 returns where the standard Onatski test usually finds one.
Concentrating an equal-weight book in stocks whose signed-correlation balance deviates most from the market beat 1/N on four indices at hand-picked thresholds.
Weighting other markets by forward validation raises Sharpe for dual-listed A and H share pairs and six US sector baskets, tested on 63 days.
Three price-only matrices drive a long-short book at Sharpe 1.06 against the market's 0.78, then 1.32 against 1.14 in a live forward test.
A composite-likelihood Hurst estimator puts log-VIX at 0.42 and beats method of moments on forecast error, by under a tenth of a percent.
Bitcoin topped 525, 546 and 534 days after the last three halvings while Pi Cycle, Mayer, MVRV and Puell extremes decayed every cycle.
Putting one Wasserstein ball on the drift prior instead of at every date raises Sharpe from about 0.35 to 0.48 on random 20-stock draws.
Gaussian boson sampling clusters for statistical arbitrage reach Sharpe 2.25, statistically indistinguishable from ordinary spectral clustering at 2.04.
Across 7,286 expected shortfall forecasts, EGARCH wins and Bayesian networks tie historical simulation, but every model fails the conditional backtest.
Choosing training window length and model class by tournament raises out-of-sample R-squared on 17 industry portfolios to 4.9%, double a short fixed window.
A two-dimensional Markov chain gives GARCH long memory with three parameters, still fitting 13 to 25 log-likelihood points worse than FIGARCH.
Signed order flow built from daily volume predicts next-month stock returns; the two Kyle lambda estimators explain almost nothing and flip sign.
Writing execution speed as a signature functional turns path-dependent statistical arbitrage into a concave quadratic program, tested on one pair for two months.
In a panel of 18 coins, institutionally backed ones absorb about a third less market-wide volatility, with the backing label assigned by hand.
